memory_candidates.content: When a set of sibling skills (e.g. skill-researcher, skill-planner, skill-implementer and their -hard variants) is supposed to implement an identical postflight pattern (like memory_candidates propagation), audit ALL siblings with a single grep across the family rather than assuming parity -- one skill silently diverging (skill-planner lacked the Stage 7a read+append that its five siblings had) can persist for a long time because postflight failures are silent (no error, just discarded data).

In this repo's hard-mode skills (skill-researcher-hard, skill-planner-hard, skill-implementer-hard), a terse 'Same as `skill-{base}` Stage N' cross-reference is the established house style for postflight stages that are structurally identical to the base skill (e.g. Stage 7a memory_candidates propagation, Stage 8 artifact linking) -- inlining a duplicate block in the hard variant would be inconsistent with this convention, not an improvement.
